title: Dasakam 27 — Kṣīrābdhimathanaṁ tathā Kūrmaavatāram
description: Durvasa’s curse weakens Indra; the devas seek Vishnu’s counsel, churn the ocean with the asuras, and receive support from the fully tortoise-formed Kurma. Vasuki releases poison, and Vishnu resumes the churning as the poet closes in prayer.

source.commentary: intake/D027/photo-captions.txt; original Facebook post metadata preserved at intake/D027/post.json

translation_note: No English verse translation was present in the supplied D027 reference bundle; translation_en is intentionally empty pending editorial review. The supplied photo captions are retained verbatim as commentary, not represented as a verse translation.

stanzas.sanskrit:
दुर्वासाः सुरवनिताऽऽप्तदिव्यमाल्यं
शक्राय स्वयमुपदाय तत्र भूयः ।
नागेन्द्रप्रतिमृदिते शशाप शक्रं
का क्षान्तिस्त्वदितरदेवतांशजानाम् ॥ २७-१ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
durvāsāḥ suravanitā”ptadivyamālyaṁ
śakrāya svayamupadāya tatra bhūyaḥ |
nāgendrapratimṛdite śaśāpa śakraṁ
kā kṣāntistvaditaradevatāṁśajānām || 27-1 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Sage Durvasa gifted a celestial Garland to Indra. Indra put the Garland on the elephant Irawatham and in-turn the elephant crushed it under its feet. The sage could not control his rage on the insult done and cursed Indra.

stanzas.sanskrit:
शापेन प्रथितजरेऽथ निर्जरेन्द्रे
देवेष्वप्यसुरजितेषु निष्प्रभेषु ।
शर्वाद्याः कमलजमेत्य सर्वदेवा
निर्वाणप्रभव समं भवन्तमापुः ॥ २७-२ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śāpena prathitajare’tha nirjarendre
deveṣvapyasurajiteṣu niṣprabheṣu |
śarvādyāḥ kamalajametya sarvadevā
nirvāṇaprabhava samaṁ bhavantamāpuḥ || 27-2 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Due to the curse, Indra became very old and weak, started to lose battles against Asuras. Devas became worried and went to Shiva and Brahma, and then collectively went to Bhagwan Vishnu and requested his intervention.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ब्रह्माद्यैः स्तुतमहिमा चिरं तदानीं
प्रादुष्यन् वरद पुरः परेण धाम्ना ।
हे देवा दितिजकुलैर्विधाय सन्धिं
पीयूषं परिमथतेति पर्यशास्त्वम् ॥ २७-३ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
brahmādyaiḥ stutamahimā ciraṁ tadānīṁ
prāduṣyan varada puraḥ pareṇa dhāmnā |
he devā ditijakulairvidhāya sandhiṁ
pīyūṣaṁ parimathateti paryaśāstvam || 27-3 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan directed devas to make peace with Asuras and churn the milk of ocean to get the divine nectar, which can keep Devas young and alive always.

stanzas.sanskrit:
सन्धानं कृतवति दानवैः सुरौघे
मन्थानं नयति मदेन मन्दराद्रिम् ।
भ्रष्टेऽस्मिन् बदरमिवोद्वहन् खगेन्द्रे
सद्यस्त्वं विनिहितवान् पयःपयोधौ ॥ २७-४ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
sandhānaṁ kṛtavati dānavaiḥ suraughe
manthānaṁ nayati madena mandarādrim |
bhraṣṭe’smin badaramivodvahan khagendre
sadyastvaṁ vinihitavān payaḥpayodhau || 27-4 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Devas made peace with the Asuras and with great pride carried the Mandara mountain for use as a churning rod. The mountain fell from their hands on the way. Bhagwan seated on Garuda, picked it up as if it were a tiny berry and installed it in the milk ocean.

stanzas.sanskrit:
आधाय द्रुतमथ वासुकिं वरत्रां
पाथोधौ विनिहितसर्वबीजजाले ।
प्रारब्धे मथनविधौ सुरासुरैस्तै-
-र्व्याजात्त्वं भुजगमुखेऽकरोः सुरारीन् ॥ २७-५ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
ādhāya drutamatha vāsukiṁ varatrāṁ
pāthodhau vinihitasarvabījajāle |
prārabdhe mathanavidhau surāsuraistai-
-rvyājāttvaṁ bhujagamukhe’karoḥ surārīn || 27-5 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: With Vasuki, the mighty serpent as the churning rope, the Devas and Asuras started to churn the ocean. Bhagwan cleverly made asuras hold the head side of the snake and devas the tail side.

stanzas.sanskrit:
क्षुब्धाद्रौ क्षुभितजलोदरे तदानीं
दुग्धाब्धौ गुरुतरभारतो निमग्ने ।
देवेषु व्यथिततमेषु तत्प्रियैषी
प्राणैषीः कमठतनुं कठोरपृष्ठाम् ॥ २७-६ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kṣubdhādrau kṣubhitajalodare tadānīṁ
dugdhābdhau gurutarabhārato nimagne |
deveṣu vyathitatameṣu tatpriyaiṣī
prāṇaiṣīḥ kamaṭhatanuṁ kaṭhorapṛṣṭhām || 27-6 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: While churning, due to self-weight, the mountain started to sink in the ocean. Helpless, Devas then prayed to Bhagwan, who incarnated as tortoise or Koorma and bore the weight of the entire mountain on its hard shell.

stanzas.sanskrit:
वज्रातिस्थिरतरकर्परेण विष्णो
विस्तारात् परिगतलक्षयोजनेन ।
अम्भोधेः कुहरगतेन वर्ष्मणा त्वं
निर्मग्नं क्षितिधरनाथमुन्निनेथ ॥ २७-७ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vajrātisthiratarakarpareṇa viṣṇo
vistārāt parigatalakṣayojanena |
ambhodheḥ kuharagatena varṣmaṇā tvaṁ
nirmagnaṁ kṣitidharanāthamunninetha || 27-7 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Bhagwan lifted up the sinking mountain on Bhagwan’s back which was harder than a thunderbolt and more than a lakh of Yojanas in width.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उन्मग्ने झटिति तदा धराधरेन्द्रे
निर्मेथुर्दृढमिह सम्मदेन सर्वे ।
आविश्य द्वितयगणेऽपि सर्पराजे
वैवश्यं परिशमयन्नवीवृधस्तान् ॥ २७-८ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
unmagne jhaṭiti tadā dharādharendre
nirmethurdṛḍham iha sammadena sarve |
āviśya dvitayagaṇe’pi sarparāje
vaivaśyaṁ pariśamayannavīvṛdhastān || 27-8 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: When the mountain was lifted up,  the Devas and Asuras all churned with great force and enthusiasm. Bhagwan entering into both of them and also into the serpent Vasuki, removed their fatigue and energised them.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उद्दामभ्रमणजवोन्नमद्गिरीन्द्र-
-न्यस्तैकस्थिरतरहस्तपङ्कजं त्वाम् ।
अभ्रान्ते विधिगिरिशादयः प्रमोदा-
-दुद्भ्रान्ता नुनुवुरुपात्तपुष्पवर्षाः ॥ २७-९ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
uddāmabhramaṇajavonnamadgirīndra-
-nyastaikasthiratarahastapaṅkajaṁ tvām |
abhrānte vidhigiriśādayaḥ pramodā-
-dudbhrāntā nunuvurupāttapuṣpavarṣāḥ || 27-9 ||
stanzas.commentary_en: Brahma, Shiva and other gods were wonder struck and sang in praise of Bhagwan, showering flowers from the heavens.

stanzas.sanskrit:
दैत्यौघे भुजगमुखानिलेन तप्ते
तेनैव त्रिदशकुलेऽपि किञ्चिदार्ते ।
कारुण्यात् तव किल देव वारिवाहाः
प्रावर्षन्नमरगणान्न दैत्यसङ्घान् ॥ २७-१० ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
daityaughe bhujagamukhānilena tapte
tenaiva tridaśakule’pi kiñcidārte |
kāruṇyāt tava kila deva vārivāhāḥ
prāvarṣannamaragaṇānna daityasaṅghān || 27-10 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
Vasuki started to emit poison from its mouth and this made Asuras very uncomfortable and the heat was experienced by Devas a little also.  as well to little. 
Bhagwan with compassion, the clouds were made to rain on the Devas but not on the Asuras.

stanzas.sanskrit:
उद्भ्राम्यद्बहुतिमिनक्रचक्रवाले
तत्राब्धौ चिरमथितेऽपि निर्विकारे ।
एकस्त्वं करयुगकृष्टसर्पराजः
संराजन् पवनपुरेश पाहि रोगात् ॥ २७-११ ॥
stanzas.stanza_roman:
udbhrāmyadbahutiminakracakravāle
tatrābdhau ciramathite’pi nirvikāre |
ekastvaṁ karayugakṛṣṭasarparājaḥ
saṁrājan pavanapureśa pāhi rogāt || 27-11 ||
stanzas.commentary_en:
After churning for long time, Nectar did not come. Only fishes and aquatic organisms were thrown out of the ocean. Bhagwan seeing the plight of Devas, started to churn the ocean with his two hands holding two ends of Vasuki..
Bhattathiri requests Bhagwan to relieve him of his ailments.
